proposals.evidence: Turner’s svapati article explicitly unites the coalescing so-/su-/sov- sleep stems and lists Hindi sonā and Gujarati sūvũ; yāti supplies the jā-/jo go auxiliary. The whole affirmative response is analysed synchronically as sleep + go in that order, with ordinary imperative vowels and western s-to-h outcomes preserved. The compound segmentation is an analysis of these survey expressions, not a claim that Turner prints each expression; no additional tense auxiliary or negative is omitted.

proposals.evidence: The complete expression consists of the so-/su(v)- sleep stem (Turner svapati) followed by the gayo/gyo/gai regional perfect auxiliary (Turner gata). Both lexical components are represented in their surface order, retaining h for s and ordinary finite ending variation. This is a modern compound-verb analysis from the whole response; forms with ambiguous standalone -ga, an extra particle, or a second elicited answer are excluded.
